video.title: Basic tasting practice in beer sensory training

read.where: Michigan’s Liquor Control Code lets an on-premises licensee give **samples to employees** for **education**, during legal hours, if they’re **21 or older**. Taste by **intensity**: start with the **lowest-ABV** beer and work up so big flavors don’t swamp delicate ones. The Brewers Association’s setup: a tasting sheet, a stemmed glass per beer, water, white paper, unsalted crackers, a dump bucket for every four tasters, and **2–3 oz** per person per beer.
read.mixup: A staff tasting isn’t a staff drink. Small pours, spit buckets, and only staff who are 21+.

read.where: Look at the **color against white paper**. **Smell** first without swirling, then **swirl** and smell again. **Sip** and hold it, breathing out through your nose. Notice the **finish** before you reach for water, then reset with a cracker. If your nose gets tired, smell your **sleeve** to reset.
read.mixup: Drinking water straight away washes out the finish. Wait a moment.

video.title: Preparing spiked beer sensory samples using Siebel Institute Sensory Training kits

read.bigIdea: Taste a fault once and you’ll know it.
read.where: Off-flavor **kits** spike beer with a known flaw. Cicerone sells kits made with **AROXA** (the single-user basic kit covers DMS, diacetyl, acetaldehyde, trans-2-nonenal, lightstruck and an infection flavor); **Siebel** kits (from Lallemand) and **FlavorActiV** are others. Spike a **neutral light lager**, work in rounds of five or six, label cups with letters, and always pour an **unspiked control** to compare against, the way Cicerone’s exams do.
read.mixup: A master kit with 24 flavors is for exam study. Floor staff need the basic six.

read.bigIdea: Catch the problem before a guest does.
read.where: The Brewers Association’s pre-shift check: **flush** faucets with clean water and wipe them with a clean towel; pour **1–3 oz** from each tap to check it works and **taste** it to confirm the tap marker matches the beer; wipe up spills; look for **fruit flies**; check glassware for **smells, dust and lipstick**. Make it part of every opening.
read.mixup: A tap marker can be wrong after a keg change. Tasting is how you catch it.
